title: Law of Parallelogram of Vectors
notes: **Statement**: If two vectors acting at a point are represented in magnitude and direction by the two adjacent sides of a parallelogram drawn from that point, their resultant is represented in magnitude and direction by the diagonal of the parallelogram passing through the same point.

**Derivation**: consider $\vec{P}$ and $\vec{Q}$ inclined at angle $\theta$, forming adjacent sides $AB$ and $AD$ of parallelogram $ABCD$. Draw $CE$ perpendicular to $AB$ extended. In right triangle $BCE$: $CE=Q\sin\theta$, $BE=Q\cos\theta$, so $AE = AB+BE = P+Q\cos\theta$.

**Magnitude**: $R=\sqrt{P^2+Q^2+2PQ\cos\theta}$. **Direction**: $\tan\alpha=\dfrac{Q\sin\theta}{P+Q\cos\theta}$ — identical results to the triangle law, since the diagonal of the parallelogram is exactly the third side of the triangle formed by $\vec P$ and $\vec Q$.
